issues.description: The UML/problem statement declares Pneumatic.raisePressure(pressureIncrease: int) but the solution's Pneumatic interface declares raisePressure(double pressureIncrease) while the solution's implementing classes (LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster) implement raisePressure(int). This creates an internal contradiction in the solution and a mismatch with the specification, which will cause compilation errors and confusion about the correct parameter type.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the parameter type for raisePressure consistent across specification and implementation. Preferably change the Pneumatic interface's method signature to void raisePressure(int pressureIncrease) so it matches the UML/problem statement and the implementing classes, or alternatively update the UML and all implementations to use double. Ensure all files use the same parameter type to avoid compilation errors.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Pneumatic.raisePressure(pressureIncrease: int) (an int parameter), but the provided solution declares Pneumatic.raisePressure(double pressureIncrease) (a double parameter). This mismatch between the problem UML and the solution API for the same method creates mapping confusion for students who are instructed to implement the interface exactly as in the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across artifacts. Change Pneumatic.raisePressure in the solution (and template) to use an int parameter (void raisePressure(int pressureIncrease)) to match the UML in problem_statement.md; or update the UML in the problem statement to use double if the intended type is double.
